sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
Braxis Holdout is a 2-lane Map belonging to the Starcraft universe.
The signature Objective of this Map are Beacons that reward Zerg Waves.
The team who wins the Objective will get a 100% power Zerg Wave,
the other team will get a less powerful one.

sections.title: Lane Assignments
sections.text:
Here you can find one or more formations
that are viable on this Map. Keep in mind that positions in lane
are not strict and will often change based on the situation.

sections.title: Formation 1-4
sections.text:
The go-to formation for Braxis Holdout is 1-4:
1 Hero, the Offlaner covers the top lane;
4 Heroes cover the bottom lane.
Use this formation to counter the 1-3-1 formation.

sections.title: Formation 2-3
sections.text:
Another good formation for Braxis Holdout is 2-3:
2 Heroes with tools to overwhelm the enemy Offlaner cover the top lane;
3 Heroes with tools to stop a push cover the bottom lane.
Use this strategy to counter the 1-4 formation.

sections.title: Formation 1-3-1
Map Strategy
sections.text:
At 0:30 minutes or right after the Zerg Waves die,
start clearing the allied Bruiser Camp and capture it as soon as possible.
To make this Mercenary Camp join the lane behind allied Minions,
capture it at 0:50 minutes or 20 seconds after a wave of Minions spawned.
At 0:45 minutes or right after capturing the allied Bruiser Camp,
start clearing the allied Siege Camp and capture it as soon as possible.
To make this Mercenary Camp join the lane in front of allied Minions,
capture it at 1:10 minutes or 10 seconds after a wave of Minions spawned.
At 1:30 minutes or whenever Beacons activate, make sure to have a durable Hero on each of them.
Secure at least one Beacon and keep control of it for as much as possible without dying.
Then, whenever your team gets an advantage, capture
the other Beacon to get progress and thus make your Zerg Wave more powerful. On the other hand,
if the enemy team has an advantage, you should retreat.
If your team wins the Objective with a big difference (such as 100% against 25%),
you should push with the allied Zerg Wave.
If it is early game,
the Offlaner can keep soaking.
If your team wins the Objective with a small difference (such as 100% against 75%),
you should defend from the enemy Zerg Wave unless you can destroy the enemy Core with it.
If it is early game,
the Offlaner can keep soaking.
If your team loses the Objective with a big difference (such as 25% against 100%),
you should defend allied Structures from the enemy Zerg Wave.
If it is early game,
the Offlaner can keep soaking.
If your team loses the Objective with a small difference (such as 75% against 100%),
you should defend allied Structures from the enemy Zerg Wave unless you can destroy the enemy Core with it.
If it is early game,
the Offlaner can keep soaking.
After about 10:00 minutes, whenever your team has an advantage
while there is no Objective to contest, you can capture the
Boss Camp and push with it.
Avoid doing it earlier if you do not have a dedicated team composition.

sections.title: Mercenary Camps
Siege Camp
sections.text:
This type of Mercenary Camp features 2 Hellbats. Once captured,
it spawns the same units fighting for your team in the corresponding lane.
When possible, push with them to get more value.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
0:30 minutes
3:00 minutes after its last capture
Baseline Experience
Experience Scaling
120 Experience
+4 Experience per minute (*)
(*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling 1 minute later.
Hellbats reduce the Armor of enemy Structures and Heroes hit
by their cleaving Basic Attacks for 3 seconds by 4 Armor per Basic Attack,
stacking 5 times, for a maximum of 20 Armor reduction.

sections.title: Bruiser Camp
sections.text:
This type of Mercenary Camp features 3 Goliaths and 1 Raven. Once captured,
it spawns the same units fighting for your team in the corresponding lane.
When possible, push with them to get more value.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
0:30 minutes
4:00 minutes after its last capture
Baseline Experience
Experience Scaling
270 Experience
+8 Experience per minute (*)
(*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling 1 minute later.
Ravens do not use Basic Attacks. Instead, they fire a Seeker Missile (5-second cooldown)
which Reveals the targeted Hero and damages them upon impact.
Ravens deal only 20 (not scaling) damage per second whereas
Goliaths deal 40 (+1 per minute) damage per second.

sections.title: Boss Camp
sections.text:
This type of Mercenary Camp features 1 Archangel. Once captured,
it spawns the same unit fighting for your team in the lane where
enemy Structures have the least amount of damage taken in total.
When possible, push with it to get more value.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
5:00 minutes
5:00 minutes after its last capture
Baseline Experience
Experience Scaling
750 Experience
+10 Experience per minute (*)
(*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling 1 minute later.
While in combat, the Archangel will use Mortar (3-second cooldown) to fire
a delayed projectile at an enemy and Bullet Storm (16-second cooldown) to fire
a barrel of missiles in a large rectangular area towards the closest enemy.
Due to being Elite, this Mercenary Camp is immune to Bribe
effects (such as Covert Mission by Nova).

sections.title: Globe Spawners
sections.text:
Braxis Holdout features 2 Globe Spawners: one above the top lane
and another below the bottom lane. They are positioned in a way that does not allow Heroes
who are controlling the nearby Beacon to easily pick up a Regeneration Globe from them.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
0:30 minutes
45 seconds after picking up a generated Regeneration Globe

Globe Spawners periodically spawns a neutral Regeneration Globe.
Unlike other Regeneration Globes, the ones generated this way do not disappear with time.
Try to pick them up when possible (without giving up the Objective) or the enemy team will get them.

sections.title: Map Objective
sections.text:
The signature Objective of Braxis Holdout consists of Beacons that reward Zerg Waves.
Heroes can claim Beacons to gain progress until they get pushed out of them.
Capturing a Beacon takes 3 seconds if it is neutral,
or 6 seconds if the enemy team has control over it.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
1:30 minutes
2:10 minutes after the Zerg Waves die

Capture the Beacons
Periodically two beacons will activate. Capture both to fill your Holding Cell with Zerg.
Fill Holding Cells
Once either Holding Cell fills, both open and unleash waves of Zerg at each team's base.
Zerg Waves
Hold out against the enemy's Zerg while helping yours. The Zerg will attack Heroes, so engage cautiously.

sections.title: Beacons
sections.text:
Beacons progress by 2% every 0.75 seconds, so going straight from 0%
to 100% takes almost 40 seconds. If you step on a Beacon that is being controlled
by the enemy team while an enemy Hero is on it, you will not be able to stop
the enemy team from getting progress. You need to push them out!

sections.title: Zerg Wave

6 Zerglings and 1 Ultralisk baseline;
1 Baneling every 10% progress;
1 Hydralisk every 24% progress;
1 Guardian every 30% progress;

Once a team reaches 100% progress, Zerg Waves for each team will spawn in opposite
lanes at the same time, starting randomly and then alternating for the rest of the game.
You can see in which lanes they will spawn by looking at the color of the cages near
the middle of each lane. The allied Zerg Wave will spawn in the lane with a blue cage
whereas the enemy Zerg Wave will spawn in the lane with a red cage.
Zergs prioritize Minions and Structures, but can also
attack Heroes. Zergs have 50% resistance from crowd-control
effects, therefore these effects will last 50% less when used on them.
Whenever they attack, Guardians and Ultralisks launch Drop Pods
(13-second cooldown) that spawn 3 Zerglings and 1 Hydralisk.
Banelings have low Health but explode when hitting non-Heroes,
dealing heavy damage around them.

sections.title: Core Ability
sections.text:
Every 4 seconds, the Core will shoot 5 Missiles at a nearby enemy Hero,
dealing 5% maximum Health as damage per missile.

sections.title: Win Conditions
sections.text:
To win the game on Braxis Holdout, you should count on
any of the following win conditions:
Map Objective,
Boss Camp.

sections.title: Tips and Tricks
sections.text:
On this Map, due to the Objective taking a long time to be won,
you can use the Healing Fountain on cooldown
instead of saving it for when the Objective spawns.
If your Hero has an Ability which allows them to jump over
impassable terrain, you can use it
to quickly rotate from a lane to another.
Choose when to contest a Beacon and when to retreat depending
on which team has an advantage
in that area. If they commit top, try to get bottom (and vice versa).
Heroes with good waveclear are the best
for defending from enemy Zerg Waves, so you should prefer sending them
on that lane, especially when the enemy team gets a lot of progress.
See our Map Guides page for further information »
